temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Temperature describes how warm or cold the air is. Humidity, air movement, clothing, and activity also affect how it feels. The project combines these conditions in PMV to describe seven thermal sensations; it does not rate air temperature alone.
temperature.advice: If you feel cold or warm, try a small change to clothing, air conditioning, or a fan, then give it time. Comfort varies, so there is no need to keep adjusting just to reach Neutral.

pmv.name: PMV thermal sensation
pmv.description: PMV estimates a group’s average thermal sensation from air and radiant temperature, humidity, air speed, activity, and clothing. Negative values indicate cooler sensations, positive values warmer ones, and values near zero neutral sensations. Individual feelings can still differ.
pmv.advice: If you feel cold or warm, try a small change to clothing, air conditioning, or a fan, then give it time. Comfort varies, so there is no need to keep adjusting just to reach Neutral.

cold.label: Cold
cold.summary: The current estimate is cold. Add clothing or adjust heating, then check how you feel after a while.
cold.detail: The current estimate is cold. Add clothing or adjust heating, then check how you feel after a while.

cool.label: Cool
cool.summary: The current estimate is cool. Add a layer if needed, especially when sitting still for a long time.
cool.detail: The current estimate is cool. Add a layer if needed, especially when sitting still for a long time.

slightly_cool.label: Slightly cool
slightly_cool.summary: The current estimate is slightly cool. Consider your clothing and activity; a light layer may help when sitting, without a large change to room temperature.
slightly_cool.detail: The current estimate is slightly cool. Consider your clothing and activity; a light layer may help when sitting, without a large change to room temperature.

neutral.label: Neutral
neutral.summary: The current estimate is near neutral for most people. If you feel comfortable too, keep your settings rather than adjusting them repeatedly.
neutral.detail: The current estimate is near neutral for most people. If you feel comfortable too, keep your settings rather than adjusting them repeatedly.

slightly_warm.label: Slightly warm
slightly_warm.summary: The current estimate is slightly warm. Try a lighter layer or a small cooling adjustment, then reassess before lowering the temperature further.
slightly_warm.detail: The current estimate is slightly warm. Try a lighter layer or a small cooling adjustment, then reassess before lowering the temperature further.

warm.label: Warm
warm.summary: The current estimate is warm. Use lighter clothing, a fan, or cooling as needed; check outdoor air and temperature before ventilating.
warm.detail: The current estimate is warm. Use lighter clothing, a fan, or cooling as needed; check outdoor air and temperature before ventilating.

hot.label: Hot
hot.summary: The current estimate is hot. Rest somewhere cooler and adjust cooling as needed, then check both the reading and how you feel.
hot.detail: The current estimate is hot. Rest somewhere cooler and adjust cooling as needed, then check both the reading and how you feel.

humidity.name: Relative humidity
humidity.description: Relative humidity is the percentage of water vapor in the air compared with saturation at the same temperature. Dry air may feel uncomfortable, while persistent dampness supports mold growth. Staying within the selected reference range helps balance comfort and moisture control.
humidity.advice: When air is dry, add moisture as needed. When damp, check bathrooms, drying laundry, or leaks, then consider exhaust ventilation or a dehumidifier. Opening windows may not help if outdoor air is also humid.

dry.label: Dry
dry.summary: The current humidity is low. If your skin or throat feels dry, consider humidification and watch the reading to avoid adding too much moisture.
dry.detail: The current humidity is low. If your skin or throat feels dry, consider humidification and watch the reading to avoid adding too much moisture.

suitable.label: Suitable
suitable.summary: The current humidity is within your selected range. Keep your routine, while checking for local dampness if windows or corners show condensation.
suitable.detail: The current humidity is within your selected range. Keep your routine, while checking for local dampness if windows or corners show condensation.

slightly_humid.label: Slightly humid
slightly_humid.summary: The current humidity is slightly high. Check condensation and moisture from drying clothes; ventilate when outdoor conditions suit, then watch for improvement.
slightly_humid.detail: The current humidity is slightly high. Check condensation and moisture from drying clothes; ventilate when outdoor conditions suit, then watch for improvement.

humid.label: Humid
humid.summary: The current humidity is high. Check moisture sources and consider dehumidification; opening windows may not help when outdoor air is also damp.
humid.detail: The current humidity is high. Check moisture sources and consider dehumidification; opening windows may not help when outdoor air is also damp.

co2.name: CO₂
co2.description: CO₂ can build up indoors as people breathe and helps indicate ventilation conditions. A sustained rise suggests a need for more fresh air. It does not represent every pollutant or replace a carbon monoxide alarm.
co2.advice: High CO₂ often points to insufficient ventilation. When outdoor air is suitable, open a window or bring in fresh air mechanically. Opening a door may help circulation, but fresh air still needs to enter. Pay closer attention when more people are present or windows stay closed.

good.label: Normal
good.summary: The current CO₂ concentration is low. Keep your ventilation routine and watch the reading when more people arrive or windows stay closed.
good.detail: The current CO₂ concentration is low. Keep your ventilation routine and watch the reading when more people arrive or windows stay closed.

moderate.label: Ventilate
moderate.summary: The current CO₂ reading suggests more ventilation. If outdoor air is suitable, open a window or use fresh-air ventilation, then check whether the reading falls.
moderate.detail: The current CO₂ reading suggests more ventilation. If outdoor air is suitable, open a window or use fresh-air ventilation, then check whether the reading falls.

poor.label: Increase ventilation
poor.summary: The current CO₂ concentration is high. Increase fresh-air supply soon; if crowded, spread activities across spaces and check readings after ventilation.
poor.detail: The current CO₂ concentration is high. Increase fresh-air supply soon; if crowded, spread activities across spaces and check readings after ventilation.

pm25.name: PM2.5
pm25.description: PM2.5 is fine airborne particulate matter generally no more than 2.5 micrometers in aerodynamic diameter. Sources include combustion, cooking, and outdoor pollution. These particles can enter the lungs; consider concentration, duration, and outdoor conditions when reducing sources or filtering air.
pm25.advice: If readings rise after cooking, incense, or smoking, reduce the smoke source, use an extractor, or run particle filtration. Check outdoor air before opening windows; polluted air can bring more particles inside.

good.detail: The concentration is low. Keep your current routine and check it from time to time.

pm10.name: PM10
pm10.description: PM10 is inhalable particulate matter generally no more than 10 micrometers in aerodynamic diameter, including PM2.5. Dust, roads, and construction can raise readings. Consider outdoor conditions when controlling dust and improving filtration.
pm10.advice: Cleaning, movement, or dusty weather can raise PM10. Damp wiping instead of dry sweeping can reduce dust. Check filtration, and limit open windows when outdoor dust is heavy.

hcho.name: Formaldehyde (HCHO)
hcho.description: Formaldehyde is a gas that may be released by panels, furniture, and other materials. Read concentrations over the averaging period required by the selected reference. If elevated, check emission sources and ventilate when outdoor conditions allow.
hcho.advice: New furniture or renovation materials may keep releasing formaldehyde. If elevated, look for sources and ventilate when outdoor air is suitable. Persistent readings may warrant professional testing. No noticeable smell does not prove levels have fallen.

tvoc.name: TVOC Index
tvoc.description: The TVOC index tracks changes in a sensor’s combined response to volatile organic compounds. It is not the concentration of one pollutant or a direct measure of toxicity or health risk. This project currently displays readings and trends without rating bands.

noise.name: Noise
noise.description: Noise readings describe sound level at the measurement location. A weighting reflects the ear’s differing sensitivity to frequencies. Effects on rest depend on duration and context; the sleep scene uses stricter boundaries.
noise.advice: If sound affects focus or rest, lower the volume, move noisy equipment, or find a quieter spot. Use the sleep scene for guidance when resting, as sound can be more disruptive then.

quiet.label: Quiet
quiet.summary: The current sound level is low for quiet activities. For rest or sleep, also consider whether sounds are steady or sudden.
quiet.detail: The current sound level is low for quiet activities. For rest or sleep, also consider whether sounds are steady or sudden.

noticeable.label: Noticeable
noticeable.summary: The current sound is noticeable and may interrupt focus or rest. If it bothers you, lower the source volume, close a door, or move somewhere quieter.
noticeable.detail: The current sound is noticeable and may interrupt focus or rest. If it bothers you, lower the source volume, close a door, or move somewhere quieter.

loud.label: Loud
loud.summary: The current environment is loud. Reduce or move away from the source, and choose a quieter place for focus or rest before checking again.
loud.detail: The current environment is loud. Reduce or move away from the source, and choose a quieter place for focus or rest before checking again.

very_loud.label: Very loud
very_loud.summary: The current environment is very loud. Limit time there and reduce the source or move somewhere quieter; duration matters as well as this reading.
very_loud.detail: The current environment is very loud. Limit time there and reduce the source or move somewhere quieter; duration matters as well as this reading.

illuminance.name: Light / Illuminance
illuminance.description: Illuminance measures visible light falling on a surface, in lux. Different activities need different levels; brighter is not always better. A single device reading is a scene hint. Check the actual task surface for reading or work.
illuminance.advice: For reading, writing, or crafts, add a light at the task location and adjust it to avoid hand shadows and glare. Light at the device may differ from the desk, so a higher number is not the goal by itself.

low_light.label: Low light
low_light.summary: At this reading, this reading is low. Add light for moving around or finding things, and check the desk surface before reading.
low_light.detail: At this reading, this reading is low. Check illuminance at the activity location. Add light for moving around or finding things, and check the desk surface before reading.

ambient.label: Ambient lighting
ambient.summary: At this reading, this reading is near the illuminance level for ambient lighting. This can support a soft atmosphere; add task lighting for reading or crafts.
ambient.detail: At this reading, this reading is near the illuminance level for ambient lighting. This can support a soft atmosphere; add task lighting for reading or crafts.

daily_activity.summary: At this reading, this reading is near the illuminance level for general activity. Use this as a reference for everyday activities; check desk lighting separately for reading or writing.

o3.name: Ozone O₃
o3.description: This is ground-level ozone, not the protective ozone layer high above Earth. It can form when other pollutants react in sunlight. At elevated levels, consult local forecasts to adjust outdoor activity timing and intensity.
o3.advice: When ozone is high, move strenuous outdoor activities such as running or cycling to a lower forecast period, or shorten them. Check outdoor ozone before opening windows; a fresh smell is not a reliable guide.

co.advice: These bands describe outdoor air quality. If a CO alarm sounds or you suspect a combustion leak, leave the affected area immediately and seek local emergency help. Do not wait for a rating change or rely only on opening windows.

so2.advice: When outdoor SO₂ is high, spend less time in affected places and move outdoor activities to a cleaner-air period. Consider outdoor readings before ventilating; opening windows may not help when levels are high.

pollen.name: Pollen
pollen.description: Pollen readings count grains per volume of air. Allergenic potential and rating thresholds differ by type and reference. Sensitive people can plan activities based on their own response. A total count without a type does not establish a load rating.
pollen.advice: If you are sensitive to pollen, read the count alongside your own reactions. When pollen is abundant, avoid leaving windows open for long and change outer clothing after going out. Different pollen types can affect you differently at the same count.

absent.label: Not detected
absent.summary: At this reading, the measured pollen count is zero. This reflects this sample, not a lasting absence nearby; check local forecasts when planning trips.
absent.detail: At this reading, the measured pollen count is zero. This reflects this sample, not a lasting absence nearby; check local forecasts when planning trips.

low.label: Low
low.summary: At this reading, the load of this pollen type is low. Plan activities around your sensitivity; a low load does not rule out individual reactions.
low.detail: At this reading, the load of this pollen type is low. Plan activities around your sensitivity; a low load does not rule out individual reactions.

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.summary: At this reading, pollen load is moderate. Check local forecasts before going out and adjust time outdoors to your own response.
moderate.detail: At this reading, pollen load is moderate. Sensitive people can watch their symptoms. Check local forecasts before going out and adjust time outdoors to your own response.

high.label: High
high.summary: At this reading, pollen load is high. If sensitive to this pollen type, shorten outdoor activities and window-opening time, and change outer clothing after outings.
high.detail: At this reading, pollen load is high. Sensitive people may wish to plan outdoor activities. If sensitive to this pollen type, shorten outdoor activities and window-opening time, and change outer clothing after outings.

very_high.label: Extreme
very_high.summary: At this reading, pollen load is extreme. If sensitive to this pollen type, reduce unnecessary exposure and use local forecasts to plan outings and ventilation.
very_high.detail: At this reading, pollen load is extreme. Sensitive people should consider protection. If sensitive to this pollen type, reduce unnecessary exposure and use local forecasts to plan outings and ventilation.

uv_index.name: UV Index
uv_index.description: The UV Index describes the potential strength of solar UV damage to skin and eyes, not visible illuminance. Higher values call for greater attention to sun protection and shade. Distinguish a current reading from the daily maximum.
uv_index.advice: Check the UV Index before heading out and prepare a hat, covering clothing, or sunscreen. At higher levels, use shade and limit midday exposure. Cool or cloudy weather does not always mean low UV.

low.label: Low
low.summary: At this reading, uV intensity is low. Consider protection for your activity; on longer outings, keep shade and changing index values in mind.
low.detail: At this reading, uV intensity is low. Consider protection for your activity; on longer outings, keep shade and changing index values in mind.

moderate.label: Moderate
moderate.summary: At this reading, uV is moderate. Bring a hat, covering clothing, and sunscreen; seek shade during longer stays outdoors.
moderate.detail: At this reading, uV is moderate. Keep exposure time in mind. Bring a hat, covering clothing, and sunscreen; seek shade during longer stays outdoors.

high.label: High
high.summary: At this reading, uV is high. Use shade and sun protection outdoors, and avoid prolonged exposure around midday.
high.detail: At this reading, uV is high. Use sun protection outdoors. Use shade and sun protection outdoors, and avoid prolonged exposure around midday.

very_high.label: Very high
very_high.summary: At this reading, uV is very high. Reschedule outdoor activities away from midday where possible, and combine covering clothing with sunscreen.
very_high.detail: At this reading, uV is very high. Limit midday exposure. Reschedule outdoor activities away from midday where possible, and combine covering clothing with sunscreen.

extreme.label: Extreme
extreme.summary: At this reading, uV is extreme. Reduce unnecessary outdoor exposure; when going out is essential, seek shelter and use comprehensive sun protection.
extreme.detail: At this reading, uV is extreme. Avoid unnecessary outdoor exposure. Reduce unnecessary outdoor exposure; when going out is essential, seek shelter and use comprehensive sun protection.

iso_7730_2025.name: ISO 7730:2025
iso_7730_2025.description: ISO 7730 explains how people experience the thermal environment, considering temperature, humidity, air speed, radiant temperature, clothing, and activity. PMV and PPD estimate a group’s thermal sensation and likely dissatisfaction. The project uses these methods to describe cooler, warmer, or near-neutral conditions.

ashrae_55_scale.name: ASHRAE Standard 55 seven-point scale
ashrae_55_scale.description: ASHRAE Standard 55’s seven-point thermal sensation scale describes Cold through Neutral to Hot, from −3 to +3. The project uses these names to make PMV easier to understand. Its continuous display bands are product rules; a label alone does not establish compliance with the full standard.
ashrae_55_scale.organization: American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE)

epa_humidity.name: U.S. EPA humidity guidance
epa_humidity.description: The US EPA’s humidity guidance helps households reduce dampness and mold, recommending indoor relative humidity of 30–50% where possible, and below 60%. This optional reference uses Dry, Suitable, Slightly Humid, and Humid messages to guide humidification, ventilation, or dehumidification.

uba_humidity.name: German UBA humidity guidance
uba_humidity.description: The German Environment Agency recommends roughly 40–60% relative humidity year-round to support ventilation and damp prevention at home. This is the project’s default humidity reference: readings below the range are Dry and those above it Humid, helping you decide whether to add or remove moisture.

eea_aqi.name: EEA European Air Quality Index
eea_aqi.description: The European Environment Agency’s Air Quality Index describes short-term pollution in six levels. It is the default for PM2.5 and PM10, with ozone and sulfur dioxide bands also available. Results describe individual pollutants, rather than a complete official European aggregate index.

hj_633_2026.name: HJ 633—2026
hj_633_2026.description: HJ 633—2026 defines China’s rules for calculating AQI, assigning pollution categories, and reporting results. The project uses its concentration boundaries for particulate matter and supported outdoor gases. Readings must match the required averaging period: hourly and daily averages are not interchangeable.
hj_633_2026.organization: Ministry of Ecology and Environment of the People's Republic of China

epa_aqi.name: U.S. EPA AQI
epa_aqi.description: The US EPA AQI reports air quality in six categories to guide pollution awareness and outdoor activities. The project offers its concentration boundaries for supported pollutants as an alternative reference. Averaging periods and numeric processing differ, so ratings may vary between references.

uba_co2_2008.name: German UBA 2008 CO₂ guidance
uba_co2_2008.description: The German Environment Agency’s CO₂ guidance uses 1000 and 2000 ppm to divide indoor ventilation conditions into three ranges. The project presents these as Normal, Ventilate, and Increase Ventilation, helping you decide when to open windows or introduce more fresh air.

who_hcho_2010.name: WHO 2010 Guidelines for Indoor Air Quality
who_hcho_2010.description: The WHO indoor air quality guidelines provide health-based references, including 0.10 mg/m³ over 30 minutes for formaldehyde. This is the project’s default formaldehyde reference. Its six display bands are product rules around that value, not categories prescribed by WHO.

gbt_18883_2022.name: GB/T 18883—2022
gbt_18883_2022.description: GB/T 18883—2022 is China’s indoor air quality standard, covering pollutant limits and test methods. Its formaldehyde limit is 0.08 mg/m³ over one hour. The project offers this optional reference with six product-defined bands; these do not constitute a full compliance test.
gbt_18883_2022.organization: State Administration for Market Regulation / Standardization Administration of China

oehha_hcho_2008.name: California OEHHA 2008
oehha_hcho_2008.description: California OEHHA’s reference exposure levels support health risk assessment. Its one-hour acute formaldehyde reference is 0.055 mg/m³. The project offers this option with six product-defined bands. It is a California health reference, not a nationwide US legal limit.
oehha_hcho_2008.organization: California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment (OEHHA)

who_noise_1999.name: WHO Guidelines for Community Noise
who_noise_1999.description: The WHO Guidelines for Community Noise address daily life, rest, and sleep using measures such as long-term equivalent sound levels. The project draws on home and sleep references for noise messages. Its four bands for current readings are product rules, not substitutes for full long-term measurements.

ies_rp_11_26.name: ANSI/IES/ALA RP-11-26
ies_rp_11_26.description: ANSI/IES/ALA RP-11-26 recommends residential lighting by space, activity, and task surface. The project uses selected illuminance levels for messages from ambient lighting to detail work. A reading at one device location does not represent lighting across a desk or an entire room.
ies_rp_11_26.organization: Illuminating Engineering Society (IES) / American Lighting Association (ALA)

nab_pollen.name: NAB pollen levels
nab_pollen.description: The US National Allergy Bureau monitors pollen concentrations by category, including trees, grasses, and weeds. The project uses daily-average boundaries for Low, Moderate, High, and Very High messages to help daily planning. Unclassified total counts cannot use a single category’s thresholds.

meteoswiss_pollen.name: MeteoSwiss pollen load classes
meteoswiss_pollen.description: MeteoSwiss distinguishes pollen types such as birch, grasses, and ragweed, with concentration boundaries reflecting allergenic potential. The project shows daily-average load classes for supported types. These are not a common EU standard or predictions of an individual’s allergic reaction.
meteoswiss_pollen.organization: Swiss Federal Office of Meteorology and Climatology

who_uv_index.name: WHO Global Solar UV Index
who_uv_index.description: The WHO Global Solar UV Index guide uses five exposure levels to explain potential effects on skin and eyes and guide sun protection. The project adopts these levels and WHO’s RGB colors. Check whether readings show the current index or daily maximum; UV Index differs from illuminance.
